title: Rheoencephalography (REG)
what: A nurse puts sensors on your head and records a weak current through the tissues. This test is still used in some countries. From the recording, the doctor judges blood filling in the head's vessels.
why: Sometimes ordered for headaches, dizziness, or blood pressure swings. Today a vessel ultrasound is more common. Your doctor will decide what you need.
duration: usually 15 to 20 minutes; the report is usually ready the same day
tell_doctor: What bothers you and for how long
What medicines you take, especially for blood pressure and blood vessels
If you had a stroke or head injury

prepare.title: Morning
prepare.text: On the test day, no coffee, strong tea, or smoking. They affect blood vessels.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually eat, but not a big meal. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Hair
prepare.text: Clean, with no styling products or hairspray.

steps: You sit or lie down and rest for a few minutes
Electrodes on an elastic band are put on your head
A recording is made at rest. You need to sit quietly
Sometimes you are asked to turn or tilt your head
Sometimes a medicine is given under the tongue and another recording is made, only if your doctor decides
feel: It does not hurt. The current is weak and you cannot feel it
The band may press a little
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
The report is usually ready the same day
Go over the results with a neurologist

faq.q: Which is better, REG or a vessel ultrasound?
faq.a: Today a head and neck vessel ultrasound is ordered more often. It shows more. Ask your doctor what suits you.
Yes. The current is very weak, and you cannot feel it.

reminders.text: REG tomorrow. In the morning, no coffee or smoking. Clean hair, no hairspray.
